reason: Value `persistent` is ReasoningEffort::Persistent; the session seeds its effort from this key unclamped, and persistent-mode instructions are injected exactly when effort == Persistent.
Managed new-thread default effort (typed ReasoningEffort, so `persistent` parses); the TUI copies it into config.model_reasoning_effort when no explicit model setting is given.
A custom catalog supplies model_messages.persistent_instructions (null = built-in, empty = disabled), experimental_supported_tools (send_user_message_async, clock) and default_reasoning_level.
Managed-policy catalog; same persistent_instructions / experimental_supported_tools / default_reasoning_level fields decide the instructions and the async-message and clock tools.
Registers the clock.sleep tool that persistent mode uses to wait between follow-up checks.
Table form of the sleep_tool feature gate for clock.sleep.
model_driven registers clock.sleep only when the catalog lists `clock` or current_time_reminder.sleep_tool is set; always_on registers it regardless.
Persistent mode auto-enables this feature with sleep_tool=true for the turn; any explicit current_time_reminder config suppresses those defaults.
Turns the clock/current-time tool on; forwarded by the desktop app to durable (Aeon) hosts alongside codex_internal_persistent_mode.
Exposes clock.sleep in model_driven mode when the reminder is on; persistent defaults set it to true.
system vs external clock; external makes the app-server client supply time and sleep deadlines for clock tools.
Which inference boundaries receive current-time reminders during long-running persistent turns.
Interval between current-time reminders injected into long-running turns.
Reports failed clock reads to the model instead of failing the turn (clock tools that persistent mode depends on).
Appends trusted response-config items when effort changes; tested for high <-> persistent transitions (wire value `disabled`).
Registers the sibling send_message_to_user_async tool for root agents without catalog support; forwarded by the desktop to durable (Aeon) hosts.
Removed predecessor flag for model-enabled async user messaging (accepted, no effect).
Goals extension continues an active goal when the thread goes idle (the 'automatic continuations' the persistent template refers to).
Settings table for goal continuation (automatic idle continuation of long-running work).
Caps the token budget of goal continuation, bounding automatic long-running follow-up work.

Desktop maps its local-automations capability to this flag; those automations (heartbeat runs that start scheduled turns in an existing thread) are the recurring-work alternative the persistent prompt names.
Keeps the machine awake while a turn is running; persistent turns stay in progress across clock.sleep waits.
